articles.headline: Sources: Injury-plagued Thunder agree to 2-year deal with veteran Dalen Terry
articles.description: Dalen Terry has agreed to a two-year deal with the Thunder, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
Dalen Terry has agreed to a two-year deal with the Oklahoma City Thunder, sources told ESPN.

Terry enters his fifth NBA season after stints with the Chicago Bulls and Philadelphia 76ers. The 6-foot-6 swingman spent the offseason training with the Golden State Warriors and went to training camp with the franchise last month.

The deal with Terry comes in the wake of the injury-plagued Thunder's reneged agreement with free agent Ochai Agbaji to fill their open roster spot with potential season-ending surgeries for Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace.

Oklahoma City star big man Chet Holmgren also is out two-plus months because of a small patellar tendon tear. The Holmgren injury prompted the Thunder to back out of their agreement with Agbaji on Friday and reconsider their options for their final roster spot.

Terry, 24, played 48 combined games last season with Chicago and Philadelphia, averaging 3.7 points and 1.8 rebounds. The 18th overall pick in the 2022 draft, Terry has averaged 3.5 points in 218 career games.

articles.headline: NBA Contract Year All-Stars: 12 playing for a payday -- and what each might get
articles.description: Bobby Marks selects a roster full of players with contract decisions that could shape the trade deadline and summer of 2027.
articles.body:
Things you might not know about Memphis Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome, the 29-year-old journeyman averaging 28 points per game for one of the NBA's most surprising teams:

Jerome played in the first 16-1 upset in NCAA tournament history, when he and Virginia were stunned by UMBC in 2018. (Jerome and the Cavaliers would win the title the next season.) He played two seasons with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in Oklahoma City. He played one season with Stephen Curry in Golden State.

Something front offices around the league are surely aware of by now: Jerome can become an unrestricted free agent next summer.

Jerome, a starting guard for ESPN's Contract Year All-Stars, headlines a 12-player roster full of potential impact free agents, many of whom are searching for massive paydays in the 2027 offseason. We're also providing early predictions on each player's next contract and the likelihood of getting moved by the February trade deadline.

Let's run down the roster.

Jump to:

Starters | Reserves

How we selected the roster

We disqualified players who have previously made an All-NBA or All-Star team. That means you won't see potential summer free agents such as the Washington Wizards' Anthony Davis, New York Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns, Miami Heat's Giannis Antetokounmpo, Milwaukee Bucks' Tyler Herro -- or even Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James, who holds a player option for 2027-28 -- on this list.

Players with team options in their current contracts, such as the Knicks' Josh Hart and LA Clippers' Rui Hachimura, also were not considered. After all, if a player is outplaying his deal enough to be considered a Contract Year All-Star, it is highly unlikely his team will decline the option.

Finally, we have kept off potential 2027 restricted free agents, such as the Detroit Pistons' Daniss Jenkins.

STARTERS

Fred VanVleet, Rockets

2026-27 stats: 12.2 PTS | 6.8 AST | 1.7 STL

Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent

Impact this season: VanVleet is averaging his fewest points per game since 2018-19 but has steadied the Rockets' offense. After missing all of last season with a torn ACL in his right knee, the 32-year-old guard is averaging 6.8 assists with only 1.0 turnovers per game. As a result, Houston's assist rate has improved from 27th in 2025-26 to 13th in the early going this season.

Prediction: The Rockets will advance deep into the playoffs and re-sign VanVleet in unrestricted free agency.

Despite being in the final year of his contract, VanVleet is not extension-eligible because he signed a two-year deal in 2025. How VanVleet factors into Houston's future could be determined by the franchise's finances. With Year 1 of Amen Thompson and Tari Eason's extensions beginning in 2027-28, Houston is projected to be $10 million below the luxury tax and $19 million below the first apron.

articles.headline: How the Knicks' season, title defense got chaotic -- fast
articles.description: New York has stayed in the headlines -- for all the wrong reasons. Can the 2026 champs bounce back?
articles.body:
THE VISUAL WAS  telling, if not stark.

The Philadelphia 76ers moved the ball all over their NBA Cup-adorned court while the New York Knicks scrambled to catch up, reminiscent of how the reigning champions ran things in the second round of last season's playoffs when they won 15 of their final 16 games, including 13 straight.

This time, the Knicks weren't taking over Xfinity Mobile Arena. They didn't get 3-pointers from Josh Hart or Miles McBride or Jalen Brunson after good ball movement. Instead, 76ers star Tyrese Maxey was driving down the lane for an easy dunk.

Sixers fans chanted "MVP" for Maxey instead of being drowned out by their rivals who made the trek down I-95. LeBron James, after a tip-in that sealed the game, basked in the love as the newest addition to this rivalry. And after Philadelphia handed New York its fourth loss of the season, a 98-93 defeat, Hart carried a bloody bruise atop his freshly braided head.

Heavy is the head that wears the crown.

If "easy" was the word used to describe the Knicks' spring, they haven't had a moment of ease since. Off the court, the team has been plagued by headlines about contract extension talks being paused for its stars until season's end and championship ring controversy. On the court, they've posted a 3-4 record, ranked 22nd in offense, and shot 35.7% from 3-point range, slightly above league average.

Early returns have the Knicks often looking like two different teams within the same night, sometimes the same quarter. Before, when the Knicks would go on one of those devastating runs of ball-popping offense and suffocating defense, teams would cower.

You could feel it. Momentum building, an almost inevitable feeling that everything would eventually go the Knicks' way -- a massive factor in their record 14.9 point differential in the playoffs.

Now, teams merely wait out the Knicks, knowing an opening is coming.

"One thing I see, when we get those runs, we start to look like the team we've been in the past. [Then] we get a little comfortable," Brunson said following the loss to the Orlando Magic. "We've got to continue to put our foot on the gas and execute like we did last year."

Coach Mike Brown didn't deny his team has gotten off to a lethargic start. His task of getting this team to repeat as champions is tough enough: The parity era of eight champions in the past eight years is the longest such stretch in NBA history. Only last season's Thunder even made it out of the second round in pursuit of defending their title. 

It could be the competition catching up to the Knicks, or the uncertainty of player contracts having a very human effect. But to his credit, Brown is focusing on the long game and not the panic that can set in with a misfortunate start to the season.

"This is a new season. It's a new team, and we're going to have challenges in front of us," Brown said. "It's like climbing a mountain. You know, sometimes you go 100 yards, but you might get knocked back 5 yards.

articles.headline: Prince William to attend Barcelona vs. Aston Villa at Camp Nou - source
articles.description: The Prince of Wales will make an away trip in support of Aston Villa, with a source confirming he plans to attend Tuesday's UEFA Champions League match against Barcelona.
articles.body:
The Prince of Wales will make another European away trip in support of Aston Villa as he plans to attend Tuesday's UEFA Champions League match against Barcelona, a source confirmed to ESPN.

William, 44, will be joined by his son, George, for the fixture against Barça at Spotify Camp Nou, the source added, as the Spanish champions make preparations for the Royal visit.

A devoted Villa supporter since childhood, the prince has attended the team's games when his schedule allows and has made a special effort to watch them in Europe in recent years.

In May, he was in Istanbul to see Villa beat Freiburg 3-0 in the Europa League final.

He was also present in Paris, accompanied by George, in 2025 for Villa's Champions League quarterfinal against Paris Saint-Germain as the Premier League side returned to the competition for the first time since 1983.

William has been a regular presence at Villa Park, too, including for the 6-0 win against Fenerbahçe last month.

Speaking to the BBC in 2015, he explained he chose to support Villa at school because most of his friends followed either Manchester United or Chelsea and he wanted something different.

"I didn't really want to follow the run-of-the-mill teams," he said.

"I wanted to have a team that was more middle of the table; that could give me the more emotional rollercoaster moments."

- Barcelona lift ban on supporters' group for Aston Villa clash

- Barcelona's Anthony Gordon ahead of Aston Villa: 'I can do a lot more'

- Aston Villa's Pau Torres relishing chance to face Lamine Yamal

Villa were in the Championship as recently as 2019, but have steadily returned to the upper echelons of English football since being back in the Premier League.

Their progress has been especially rapid under coach Unai Emery, who helped them return to the Champions League -- a competition they won in 1982 when it was known as the European Cup -- in 2024.

They were eventually knocked out by PSG in the last eight that year, but went on to win the Europa League last season and are back in the Champions League this term.

Villa have won all three of their games in the league phase so far, but will face their toughest test yet against LaLiga leaders Barça.

articles.headline: Fantasy buzz: No stopping Bears, Seahawks ease Charbonnet back, Minshew impact
articles.description: The Bears' offense is full of must-start players, Seahawks backfield still in flux as Charbonnet, Price return
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Nov. 3: Bears roster full of must-starts, Seahawks ease Charbonnet back into mix

By Michael F. Florio

The Bears' offense continued rolling on the road against the Super Bowl champs. D'Andre Swift was the star of the show, turning 30 opportunities into 79 yards and three touchdowns. He finished with 23 fantasy points and surely saved many fantasy teams from the jaws of defeat. Luther Burden III stayed hot, turning nine targets into seven catches for 56 yards and a touchdown. He finished with 18.6 fantasy points and has averaged 19.9 fantasy points per game since Caleb Williams returned. He has emerged as the Bears' top pass catcher and is a weekly start. Colston Loveland also saw nine targets, catching seven of them for 65 yards. He finished with 11.5 fantasy points. He has averaged 16.6 fantasy points per game since Williams returned. He is a must-start option each week.

Williams played extremely well even if it did not translate to the biggest fantasy game. He was the first QB to throw for more than 200 yards against the Seahawks' defense. In total he finished with 13.98 fantasy points. That is more about the matchup, though. Williams should be started weekly.

Rome Odunze saw six targets, catching four of them for 87 yards. His 12.7 fantasy points is his second-highest mark in a game this season. It's great to see Odunze produce, but he remains the third target. That makes him a low-floor, high-upside flex option.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to be the Seahawks' offense. He saw 11 targets, catching six for 118 yards and a touchdown. He should be in MVP talks and should be viewed as the best WR in fantasy football. He has one game with fewer than 22 fantasy points this season. He has 52% of his teams receiving yards -- no other player even has 40%.

Both Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet returned from injury in Week 9. Price led the way playing 48% of snaps, with 10 carries and four targets. He finished with 37 yards and 5.7 fantasy points. Charbonnet played 36% of snaps, with six carries and four targets. He went for 29 yards and finished with 5.9 fantasy points. They have a better matchup next week against the Cardinals, but splitting the usage leaves them both as purely flex options.

Sam Darnold's struggles continued, but he ended up having a solid fantasy night as Seattle was trailing and had to throw. He finished with 188 passing yards, two touchdowns, one interception and 17.52 fantasy points. Darnold has nine interceptions in his past six games. articles.headline: Cleats, controversy and the choice of Bears QB Caleb Williams
articles.description: Williams wore Caddix cleats Monday night in Seattle, but the logo was not visible as he tries to 'calm things down.'
articles.body:
It was a letter Jack Rasmussen had been anticipating. The founder of Caddix, a cleats start-up that has squeezed its way into NFL locker rooms, knew that at some point the league would fine a player for wearing his shoes.

Then, on Oct. 20, it arrived.

The recipient was Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who was fined $11,941 for wearing an "unauthorized logo" on his cleats in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons. On Thursday, the league fined Williams again, this time for $23,882, for wearing the Caddix footwear in Week 7 against the New England Patriots.

All Williams had to do to avoid the fines -- which Caddix and company investor Joe Flacco said they were willing to pay -- is cover up the logo. Williams told ESPN last week that wasn't in his plans for Monday night's game against the Seattle Seahawks, but he changed his mind, saying he wanted to "calm things down" for his team. He wore matte black cleats that did not show the Caddix logo. Williams had another strong game in a 34-17 victory.

This season has been Caddix's breakthrough. After passing NFL testing in May 2025, Caddix was approved earlier this year as a non-licensed footwear company, allowing the cleats to be worn during games. But non-licensed footwear brands can't have their logos visible on the field.

Companies pay the NFL millions of dollars to be allowed to show their logo and, as of now, that list includes just three brands: Nike, Adidas and Under Armour.

Williams, who does not have an endorsement deal with Caddix, said there were times when his feet, ankles and knees would hurt when wearing footwear in the past. And after pitches from multiple footwear companies, he chose not to sign a deal with any of them. That led Caleb's dad, Carl, to ask Williams' longtime quarterbacks coach Tom Gormely if there were any other cleat companies to consider.

He knew of one, a small start-up whose moveable cleats were designed to help prevent injury. Rasmussen said prototypes were developed about 12 years ago, and the company was incorporated in 2023. Flacco was the first NFL player to wear them on the field in 2024 while he was with the Indianapolis Colts.

In August 2025, Gormely called Rasmussen with a vague message: He had an NFL quarterback as a client who was looking for new cleats.

About a month later, after Gormely vetted the technology and the cleats, he told Rasmussen who they were for. As a small brand fighting for a sliver of the NFL cleat market, Rasmussen knew what having a player the caliber of Williams wearing his cleats could do for his brand. However, Gormely didn't want Williams to switch over to Caddix at the start of the 2025 season.

Williams started working out in Caddix this offseason. He sprinted, cut and pivoted in them, and trained inside and outside. Throughout their sessions, Williams would provide feedback to Gormely, who would then share it with Caddix.

articles.headline: RB Leipzig's Maxime Estève on his plan to stop 'best striker' Erling Haaland
articles.description: RB Leipzig's Maxime Estève has opened up about how he plans to try and stop Erling Haaland and banishing the memories of a painful defeat to Man City when he was at Burnley.
articles.body:
Training sessions against his managers and former Manchester City players Vincent Kompany and Martin Demichelis showed RB Leipzig defender Maxime Estève the competitive standards required to play Champions League football and he'll take those lessons into his next challenge: Stopping Erling Haaland on Wednesday.

Centre back Estève, 24, joined Bundesliga side RB Leipzig from Burnley for €25 million in the summer. He's played for his new side in the German topflight, but Estève is still waiting for his Champions League debut, and he is hoping that could come against Manchester City at the Etihad on Wednesday.

If he gets the nod against City, then his primary challenge will be to stop City star Haaland, who already has 13 goals in all competitions this season. Estève already has first-hand experience of playing Haaland from his time with Burnley, where he played from 2024 to 2026.

"I played twice against him and he's the best striker in the world at this point along with Harry Kane," Estève told reporters on Monday. "In a few years' time he'll still be in this position: he's so powerful, so good at heading, so quick, and he has all the qualities to be a beast. But to progress in football, you must play against the best opponents so it's a good challenge to play against these opponents and types of players."

Estève says Haaland's patience and movement makes him hard to mark. "I remember when I played against him, he waits, and they have other players like Rayan Cherki who play in the small spaces, so he tries to stay around but they have their habits. They can chip the ball to the far post, and he can come in aggressively with a big header.

"He's not that active with the ball, but every time he does touch the ball, you have to be focused 100% because, you know, in one second, he can score. He's a difficult player to mark.

"He's a really good finisher and he adapts his game the whole time. So for me, he's the best striker I've played against."

If Estève wants any advice on what it takes to tame the world's greatest strikers, then he can take inspiration from managers he's played under. Estève signed for Burnley in February 2024 on loan and worked under ex-City great Kompany for the remainer of the 2024-25 season.

That summer, Kompany left to take charge of Bayern Munich but Estève signed a permanent deal and stayed at Burnley for a further two seasons before joining Leipzig in July 2026. There he has ex-Argentina center back Demichelis as manager, after the Argentinean defender took over in June.

articles.headline: Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 9: Bucs atop NFC South? RB trades coming?
articles.description: Get ready for Week 9 with takes on the Bucs' division chances, why RBs could dominate the trade deadline and which teams should at least ask about Justin Herbert.
articles.body:
Are you excited for NFL Week 9? It's the last week before the trade deadline next Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. It's also the official midway point of the season. Feel that little bite in the air? Playoff football will soon cometh.

Every Tuesday of the NFL season, I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide'

This week, I'll start with my headliner expectation for the 2026 trade deadline, irresponsibly put my faith in a 3-5 Buccaneers team and wonder just how much the Chargers would get if they traded Justin Herbert.

Jump to:

RB trades are coming before the deadline

Cowboys should trade Pickens

Irving will lead the Bucs to NFC South title

Steelers are going to win the AFC North

Three teams should try to trade for Herbert

Campanile will be a head coach candidate

Bears could be dangerous with Simmons

Some extra trade inklings

I think ... the running back movement will be the story of the trade deadline 

The splashiest name included in the 2026 NFL trade deadline rumor mill is Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.

He is a special player who can have the same impact on a healthy offense that Saquon Barkley had for the Eagles in 2024 and Derrick Henry for the Ravens in the same year. Barkley and Henry had rushing success rates of 35.4% and 37.8%, respectively, and averaged 4.2 and 4.3 yards per carry, respectively, in the two seasons before they joined their new squads. Over the past two seasons, Taylor has a 41.2% success rate and is averaging 4.7 yards per pop. His recent body of work, along with the glimmer of elite play we saw in the early parts of the 2025 season, indicates that he can be a transformative addition.

 

As such, the Colts are -- unsurprisingly -- demanding a big return for Taylor. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Colts' asking price is something in line with the Christian McCaffrey trade package from 2023 -- a second-round pick, a third-round pick and some more capital.

If Taylor gets dealt for that much compensation to a team such as the Vikings, Giants, Broncos or Bengals (or a surprise team such as the Packers and Seahawks), it's possible the running back trade market will freeze up. If the Colts get that much in return for Taylor, what could the Titans get for Tony Pollard or the Jets for Breece Hall?
